title: Sluggish random walks with resetting: nonequilibrium aspects
authors: Theophilus Dwamena Frimpong, Léa Bresque, Edgar Roldán
abstract: We derive exact analytical expressions for the fixed-time probability distribution and the Laplace transform of the distribution of the first-passage time to reach a target for a sluggish random walk in one dimension subject to two different types of stochastic resetting: stochastic resetting at random Poisson-distributed times, and resetting implemented whenever a position threshold is reached. The optimal resetting rate that minimises the mean first-passage time is obtained as a function of the sluggishness parameter, while under threshold resetting the mean first-passage time to the origin is found to increase monotonically with the threshold. We also characterise the occupation-time statistics, retrieving a Lamperti-type distribution under free dynamics and under Poissonian resetting at rate for short observation times, a Gaussian distribution centred at half for long observation times, and a distinct deterministic limit under threshold resetting. To further characterise nonequilibrium aspects of resetting, we evaluate the distribution and mean of the cost incurred per reset under Poissonian resetting, and the cost rate under threshold resetting, for different (linear, power-law, exponential) cost functions, and find the same critical behaviour of the cost rate in the limits of a vanishing resetting rate and an infinite threshold, respectively. Numerical simulations validate with excellent accuracy our analytical formulae.
summary: This paper provides rigorous analytical solutions for sluggish random walks subjected to stochastic resetting. It analyzes two types of resetting—Poissonian and threshold-based—deriving exact expressions for key observables like first-passage times and stationary distributions. The work is significant for understanding how non-Markovian or non-equilibrium processes modify fundamental transport phenomena in complex systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the non-equilibrium dynamics of sluggish random walks subjected to two distinct stochastic resetting protocols: Poissonian and threshold-based.
main_result: Exact analytical expressions are derived for the first-passage time distribution and stationary states under both resetting types, revealing how sluggishness modifies critical exponents and cost behaviors.
method: The authors employ analytical derivations, solving modified Fokker-Planck equations, utilizing Laplace transforms, and applying renewal theory to characterize the system's time evolution.
model_or_system: The model is a sluggish random walk in one dimension, described by a position-dependent diffusion coefficient $D(x) \propto |x|^{-\alpha}$. The dynamics are perturbed by either Poissonian resetting at rate $r$ or resetting upon reaching a threshold $x_{th}$.
key_observables: Fixed-time probability distribution, Laplace transform of first-passage time, occupation-time statistics (Lamperti/Gaussian), and the cost rate associated with resetting.
important_parameters: Sluggishness parameter ($\alpha$), resetting rate ($r$), and threshold position ($x_{th}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the continuum limit approximation for the underlying discrete Markov chain dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dynamics, showing the cusp at $x=0$ for $\alpha > 0$ and the bimodal nature of the stationary distribution for $\alpha > 0$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the governing equations for the sluggish walk, then analyzes the stationary states and first-passage times for Poissonian resetting, followed by an analysis using renewal theory for threshold resetting, concluding with a detailed comparison of the cost rate behavior in both limits.
why_interesting: The study of non-equilibrium dynamics, especially how external forcing (resetting) modifies transport properties like diffusion and relaxation times, is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum measurement theory.
